summary: Tested auth feature end-to-end (backend + frontend). 5/6 backend auth tests pass; brute force lockout does NOT trigger against the public URL because the app runs behind 2 backend pods and lockout identifier uses request.client.host (per-pod peer IP), so failed attempts split across pods and never reach 5 on any single identifier. All frontend flows (login, signup, forgot/reset, logout, guest close/X close, admin badge) passed. Guest dashboard + Route Analyze regression passed.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout bypassed in production: identifier uses request.client.host which differs between the 2 backend pods (10.49.134.136 / 10.49.139.194). Verified in DB: attempts split across pods, neither reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=5. Fix: derive client IP from X-Forwarded-For header (fallback to request.client.host) OR key lockout on email only.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout identifier to use X-Forwarded-For (or first IP in chain) so lockouts aggregate across pods; consider also keying purely on email to prevent trivial IP-rotation bypass.
(Carryover) Remove hardcoded fallback defaults for MONGO_URL/DB_NAME/JWT_SECRET/ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD in backend/auth.py & server.py; fail-fast on missing env.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py uses request.client.host for rate-limit identifier, unsafe behind ingress + multi-pod setup (see backend_issues.critical).
auth.py hardcodes fallback admin password 'admin123' if ADMIN_PASSWORD env missing — potential security risk if env is ever unset.
set_auth_cookies always sets Secure+SameSite=none which is correct for cross-site preview URL, but will break local http testing; acceptable for this deployment.
forgot-password returns reset_token in JSON — explicitly documented prototype behavior, ensure this is gated behind an env flag before production.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Only outstanding issue is brute-force lockout in multi-pod deployment. Frontend auth flows are fully functional. Duplicate email (400), token reuse (400), logout cookie clear, forgot/reset all pass. Signup auto-login and reset-password auto-fill token work in UI.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout uses identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. In this Kubernetes deployment there are 2 backend pods; request.client.host is the immediate peer (ingress-side) IP which differs per pod. Mongo shows attempts split: {pod_A_ip}:email count=3, {pod_B_ip}:email count=4. Neither identifier reaches 5, so check_lockout never triggers 429. Reproduction: register a fresh user, POST /api/auth/login with wrong password 7 times — all return 401 instead of 429 on the 6th. Mitigation: use X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or drop IP from key entirely.
